Gas just dropped below $4 for the first time since July — and it still costs more than last Thanksgiving.

The national average hit $3.78 a gallon today, down from $4.31 a month ago (AAA). A year ago it was $3.07 — so you're paying about 23% more to fill up than last November.

Airfare's worse: AAA members pay about $800 round-trip now, up 17% from a year ago.

For the first time since 2008, AAA expects fewer Thanksgiving travelers: 81.5 million, just under last year.

My take: a sub-$4 pump price makes a great headline, but the bill against last year still went up.

Driving, flying, or staying home this year?
